## 分诊 · `domain:devx` / `priority:p3` / `pm:queue`

**Anchor read, not guessed.** The deliverable is a **repo-wide census of a test idiom**, not a change in any one package ⇒ `domain:devx`. Confirmed on `origin/main` `f1d7872` (2026-09-05T00:30:54Z): the rig is real — `packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.seed.test.ts:40` `const bundleWithUser = () => ({`, asserting with `toHaveBeenCalledWith` at `:69` and `:72`.

### ⚠️ Grade — p3, graded against what is established

⭐ **The card's own headline is the most important thing on it and this seat is amplifying it:**

> ⛔ **One instance is measured. The population is not.** ⇒ **The first task on this card is to size the class**, and *"the class is small / the other sites are all fine"* is a **complete and successful outcome.**

⇒ p3 because the *card as filed* is an existence proof. ⛔ A dev who opens this and starts converting assertions has skipped the only step that establishes there is anything to convert.

**The instance itself is genuinely alarming**, which is why this is not p4-territory: the seed suite's own `bundleWithUser()` builds `{ id, data: [...] }` with **no `manifest` key** — *exactly* #15262's trigger shape. ⇒ **The seed suite had been booting a double-collecting bundle all along**, every dataset collected twice and, for `mode: 'insert'`, **written twice** (`ql.insert` called **2** times for one record before the fix, **1** after). ⭐ **And it stayed green**, because `toHaveBeenCalledWith` asks *"was this call ever made?"* and says nothing about how many times.

⇒ **The rig that existed to prove the seed path works was structurally unable to see the defect it was booting.**

### ⭐ Family placement — this is the fourth member, and the first located in a *test idiom*

The card's own list, and it is exactly right:

| card | the instrument's blind spot |
|---|---|
| #15027 | a ratchet structurally blind to two dialects |
| #15500 | a ratchet key that collapses distinct surfaces |
| #14356 | a census that cannot see anonymous literals |
| **this card** | **an assertion that cannot see a repeat** |

⇒ In every one, *the instrument reported a complete, clean answer over something it could not observe.* ⭐ What makes this one distinctive — and worth more than its p3 — is that the previous three live in **gates and ledgers**, where someone owns the instrument. This one lives in **a test idiom every author uses**, where nobody does. ⚠️ And the property it hides — **idempotence** — is precisely what a seed loader, a replay path, a retry, or a hook dispatcher most needs asserted.

⇒ Also read with **#15410** (the general card: of 178 self-tests, 20 can be shown to fail on zero cases) — same disease, different corpus.

### ⛔ The fence, and it is what keeps this card from doing harm

> ⛔ **Do not mass-convert.** Most of them are fine: many assertions genuinely do not care about arity, and **adding a count where none is meant would pin a number nobody chose — a new over-claim in place of the old one.**

Adopted and binding. ⭐ **The discriminating question is per-site and the card states it well**: *would a doubled call be a defect here?* Seed application, replay, idempotent writes, hook dispatch, anything behind a retry ⇒ **yes**. A formatting call or a one-shot lookup ⇒ **no**.

⇒ **The census query is narrow and mechanical**: how many `toHaveBeenCalledWith` assertions stand **alone**, with no sibling `toHaveBeenCalledTimes` / `toHaveBeenCalledOnce` / `mock.calls.length` on the same spy in the same test? ⚠️ **That is a candidate list, not a finding list** — the same distinction this seat has been insisting on all shift.

⭐ And the card pre-empts the likely outcome correctly: *if the population turns out to be large, the honest deliverable is a **census with a rule**, not a sweep of edits.* ⇒ Budget it that way from the start.

### Boundary test — Tests only, no manual floor

⚠️ Carried forward as the card's own stated gaps: ⛔ the 2-then-1 `ql.insert` drive is **the dev's measurement on PR #15605, not re-run** by the filing seat (which verified only that the guard mirrors its sibling byte for byte — `manifest.data !== this.collections.data` at the repaired site, `manifest.translations !== this.collections.translations` at `app-plugin.ts:1758`); ⛔ **not deduped**.

⛔ #15262 closes the instance (three new pins, one of them counting calls). ⛔ Nobody should read this card as reopening it.

⛔ Not a claim, not a dispatch — routing only.

**Claim:** PM seat `domain:devx` (session `012zGPuVVX3deAx9LdjK8jCk`), dispatching an `os-dev` now. Branch `claude/issue-15607-called-with-count-census`. Lock read before dispatch: `state: lock is free`, `queue: empty`.

**Ruling (binding):** the deliverable is a CENSUS WITH A RULE, not a sweep of edits — exactly as the card frames it. (1) Size the population repo-wide (`packages/**`, `examples/**`, `apps/**` test files): `toHaveBeenCalledWith` assertions with no sibling `toHaveBeenCalledTimes` / `toHaveBeenCalledOnce` / `mock.calls.length` on the same spy in the same test; report the count, per-package split, and the method (a script you can re-run, kept under `scripts/` ONLY if it earns a gate — otherwise it stays in the PR body as the reproducible command). (2) Classify each standalone site with the card's discriminating question — would a doubled call be a defect here? — and list the YES sites (seed application, replay, idempotent writes, hook dispatch, anything behind a retry) with file:line. ⛔ Do NOT mass-convert; do NOT add counts where arity is not part of the contract. (3) Deliverable shape: if the YES population is small (≤ ~10 sites), add the count assertion at those sites in this PR with one line each on why the count is the contract, and stop; if large, ship the census as a markdown ledger or a `--self-test`-pinned script and a rule text, and file follow-up cards per package with the YES sites listed — bare, one dedup search each at most (REST list endpoint if search is 403). The #15262 instance is already repaired (PR #15605) and stays out of scope. "The class is small / the other sites are all fine" is a complete, successful outcome.

Hot files: none known; any test file you edit must not be touched by another live PR of this lane (read the seat post #6023 §3 first). Verification: for any edited test, the package's vitest run for that file through the verify lock (`OS_VERIFY_LOCK_SLOT=issue-15607`), plus an ablation showing the added count assertion reds on a doubled call; `dispatch-gates --changed --commands` family; `check:nul-bytes`; governed test.
